summary:
Desk SYS checked the forecast's seat law against the statute and measured what the law does on the official record. The model's Bader-Ofer implementation is legally sound. The Knesset Elections Law sets the threshold at 3.25% of all valid votes (s.81(a), from Amendment 62 of 11 March 2014, in force since 2015). It uses an integer quota and floor seats, then hands out the remaining seats by highest averages, with a CEC lottery for ties (s.81(b)-(d)). A surplus agreement links one list to exactly one other, must be filed by the 11th day before the election (16 Oct 2026) and is published by the 8th (19 Oct). It counts only at the remainder stage and only if both partners pass on their own. The pair's joint seats are then split by the same method (ss.67, 82). Re-implementing ss.81-82 in exact arithmetic on the CEC's final counts reproduces the official allocation of all six 3.25%-era elections. The model's D'Hondt-on-factions code gives the identical result in 6/6, with no ties. The model's only formal departures, column-order tie-breaking and the missing majority clause s.81(d)(4), have no measurable effect.

The measured record corrects several numbers the forecast states. Between 3 and 8 seats per election are decided at the remainder stage (mean 5.3), not 6-9. Surplus pairs moved exactly one seat in 4 of 6 elections. Pair by pair, 9 of 23 effective pairs gained a seat, and the expected value is about +0.4 seat per pair (range 0.23-0.77). That matches the model's own 2026 figure (+1 in 30-35% of draws) and D'Hondt's large-list bias (Schuster et al. 2003), but not the site's '+0.5 to +0.9'.

Disproportionality in Israel is threshold waste. Gallagher's index (0.86 in 2020, 4.40-4.45 in 2019a/2022, which the desk reproduces exactly) tracks the wasted share (0.8% to 8.8%). The two high-waste elections were decided by margins of 1,454 votes (New Right 2019a) and 4,062 (Meretz 2022).

Double envelopes were 5.5% of valid votes in 2019a and 9.6% in 2021-2022: 462,807 cast in 2022 per the CEC file, not the 'over 600,000' reported in election week. 2026 adds a new legal category: evacuees vote in outer envelopes at designated stations (ch.10-3C, 5786). The envelopes cut Arab lists by 1.5-7.7 pp and UTJ by about 2-2.6 pp relative to regular stations, and favour right-religious lists. Yet from the complete regular count to the final count, the net bloc change was zero in four of five elections and -1 for the Netanyahu bloc in 2022. Meretz and Balad were already below 3.25% before the envelopes were opened.

Two implementation challenges follow. (1) The threshold test runs on shares renormalised over the 20 modelled lists. The law's denominator also includes the micro-lists, historically 0.3-0.9% of valid votes. That makes the model's threshold about 0.01-0.03 pp too lenient, of the order of the 2019a New Right miss. (2) The validation harness's historical surplus pairs are approximations that differ from the registered agreements in 2015, 2019a, 2019s and 2021. On exact official counts they misallocate 8 list-seats, so part of the graded error is seat-law error. Both fixes are cheap and testable on the harness.

findings.claim: The legal threshold is 3.25% of ALL valid votes, tested per list ('not less than'); only lists that pass take part in the allocation, and the quota is the INTEGER part of the passing lists' valid votes divided by 120; each list first receives the integer part of votes/quota.
findings.quant: s.81(a): 'not less than 3.25% (three and a quarter per cent) of all the valid votes'; s.81(b): quota = whole number of (sum of valid votes of participating lists)/120; s.81(c): seats = whole number of votes/quota. 2022: quota 36,227 (Kenig 2026, reproduced exactly from CEC counts).

findings.claim: Remainder seats go one at a time to the largest 'list quotient' votes/(seats+1); an exact tie is broken by a lottery run by the CEC; and a list with no more than half of the participating valid votes stops receiving seats once it holds half of all seats. The model breaks ties by column order (np.argmax) and does not implement the majority clause.
findings.quant: s.81(d)(1)-(3) highest-averages iteration; s.81(d)(2) tie -> 'a lottery conducted by the Central Committee'; s.81(d)(4) majority clause (cap at 60 seats for a list with <=50% of participating votes). Exact ties on the CEC counts 2015-2022: 0 of 6 elections. In the model, shares are continuous floats, so exact ties have probability ~0; the largest 2026 list is ~19% (Likud mean share 0.190), so s.81(d)(4) is unreachable.

findings.claim: Surplus-vote agreements ('linkage', התקשרות): a list may link with only ONE other list; written notice signed by both lists' agents must reach the CEC no later than the 11th day before election day; the CEC publishes the linkages by the 8th day. Linked lists act as one list ONLY in the remainder stage (combined votes and combined s.81(c) seats), and only if EACH passed the threshold on its own; their joint seats are then split between them by the same s.81 method.
findings.quant: s.67(a) one partner only; s.67(b) deadline day 11 = Friday 16 Oct 2026 for the 27 Oct election; s.67(c) publication by day 8 = 19 Oct 2026; s.82(a) 'provided that each of them by itself received the percentage of votes fixed in s.81(a)'; s.82(b) internal split by the s.81 method. Statutory amendment history of ss.67/81 includes 5733 (1973), the Bader-Ofer amendment.

findings.site_use: Signed surplus-vote agreements are treated as joint lists at the remainder stage, and only when both partners pass the threshold (s.82(a)).

findings.claim: Bader-Ofer as legislated (integer quota, floor seats, highest averages, linked lists pooled for the remainder stage, internal split) is mathematically D'Hondt applied to 'factions' (pairs pooled), and the model's implementation reproduces every official seat allocation 2015-2022 exactly.
findings.quant: Desk re-implementation of ss.81-82 in exact integer arithmetic on CEC final counts with the registered agreements: equals the official seats in 6/6 elections (2015, 2019a, 2019s, 2020, 2021, 2022); simulate.dhondt + form_factions on the same counts equals the statutory result in 6/6; 0 ties. The CEC guide describes the floor stage 'then ... the Bader-Ofer method'; Kenig (IDI 2026) calls the remainder stage D'Hondt (2022: 7 remainder seats).

findings.site_use: Threshold failures redistribute their votes to survivors, which is how a bloc can lose the vote and win the Knesset (2022: some 300,000 votes wasted; the Netanyahu camp won 64 seats on a ~30,000-vote edge).

findings.claim: Israel's disproportionality is driven by threshold waste, not by the D'Hondt formula: the Gallagher least-squares index tracks the wasted-vote share almost one-for-one across the 3.25% era.

findings.site_use: The threshold has been 3.25% of valid votes since the 2015 election (Amendment 62, March 2014); it was 2% before.

findings.claim: The threshold rise reshaped Arab-list strategy: under the 2013 shares two of the three Arab lists would have failed 3.25%, and they ran jointly in 2015 (13 seats, up from 11), but the alliance has since split and re-formed, so the threshold creates merger incentives rather than a stable merged party.
findings.quant: 2013 (2% threshold): Hadash 2.99%, Balad 2.56%, Ra'am-Ta'al 3.65%; 11 seats combined. 2015 Joint List 446,583 votes = 10.61%, 13 seats (CEC). 2019a separate: Ra'am-Balad 3.334% (passed by 3,614 votes); 2022 three-way split: Balad 2.91% failed. Eizenberg & Harsgor (2017) analyse the threshold change and its effect on Arab representation in 2015 (topic per the IDI summary; full text not opened); Plesner (IDI 2015) names the Joint List as the most prominent behavioural effect.

source.title: Apples and Oranges: Putting Electoral Thresholds in Context

findings.site_use: new claim: 'The 2014 threshold rise is why the Arab parties' fate turns on alliances: two of three Arab lists of 2013 would have fallen short of 3.25%.'

findings.claim: Israel is the textbook 'extreme' PR system (one 120-seat national district, closed lists), and the threshold rise did not durably cut fragmentation: the effective number of electoral parties fell from 8.68 (2013) to 5.19 (2020) and rebounded to 8.92 (2021) and 7.99 (2022).
findings.quant: Gallagher Eff Nv / Eff Ns: 2013 8.68/7.28; 2015 7.71/6.94; 2019a 6.33/5.24; 2019s 6.11/5.57; 2020 5.19/5.01; 2021 8.92/8.52; 2022 7.99/6.51. Rahat & Hazan: a closed-list PR system 'so proportional' that it produced a fragmented parliament (abstract); Hazan, Itzkovitch-Malka & Rahat (2017) treat Israel as 'a prototype of an extreme PR system' (abstract).

source.title: Israel: The Politics of an Extreme Electoral System
source.venue: in M. Gallagher & P. Mitchell (eds), The Politics of Electoral Systems, Oxford University Press, ch. 16, pp. 333-351 (abstract read; full text not opened)

findings.model_link: Context for the many-straddler structure of 2026 (21 latent lists, 38 filed): a fragmented field under a 3.25% bar keeps several lists in the threshold band every cycle.
findings.site_use: new claim: 'Israel elects all 120 members in one national district - one of the most proportional systems in the world - so a handful of lists near 3.25% decide the majority.'

findings.claim: Invalid ballots are excluded from every denominator; they run at 0.5-1.0% of votes cast and are defined by statute (identifying marks, more than three identical slips or slips for different lists, non-official envelope, blank slips).
findings.quant: Invalid share of votes cast (CEC): 2015 1.03% (43,854), 2019a 0.71%, 2019s 0.64%, 2020 0.54%, 2021 0.59%, 2022 0.62% (29,851 of 4,794,593). 2013: 40,904 (about 1%) disqualified (Knesset RIC/CEC leaflet). Grounds: s.78(a); CEC guide: 'two or three ballots for the same list ... valid'; blank slips without list letters invalid. s.84 requires the published results to list invalid votes separately.

findings.model_link: Model shares are shares of valid votes (vote intention); invalid voting is correctly not modelled as a list. No change.
findings.site_use: Shares are of valid votes; invalid ballots (about 0.6% in 2022) count toward turnout but not toward any list or the threshold.

findings.claim: The threshold denominator in law is ALL valid votes, including votes for the many micro-lists the model does not carry; the model renormalises shares over its modelled lists, which makes its threshold effectively 3.25% x (1 - m) of valid votes - slightly lenient, by roughly 800-1,300 votes in 2026 terms.
findings.quant: Valid-vote share of lists under 0.3% (closest analogue of the 2026 unmodelled set): 2015 0.41%, 2019a 0.80%, 2019s 0.64%, 2020 0.38%, 2021 0.28%, 2022 0.85%; lists under 0.5%: 0.41-1.49% (2022 1.49%). Ballots: 25-40 lists (2026: 38 filed; 20 latent columns in mixture_shares.csv summing to 1.000). Bias = 3.25% x m = 0.009-0.028 pp (~450-1,350 votes at ~4.8M valid) - the same order as New Right's 2019a miss (1,454 votes). Normal approximation to the 8 Oct mixture: P(pass) inflated by ~0.2-0.5 pp at m=0.3-0.7% and ~1.1-1.2 pp at m=1.5% for RZP-Zehut and Ra'am.

findings.claim: Double-envelope (outer-envelope) votes are cast by soldiers, voters at accessible stations, hospital patients, prisoners, diplomats, shelter residents and - new for 2026 - evacuees displaced since 7 October 2023; they are checked for double voting after polls close and counted centrally in the Knesset after the regular count, and the official results must be published within eight days.
findings.quant: Law: s.91(b) soldiers; s.68A(e)(1) mobility-limited voters at accessible stations (self-declaration); ch.10-3C ss.116Y10-116Y13 (amendment 5786/2026): evacuees ('a person who left his place of residence due to the security situation since 7 October 2023 and has not returned') vote at designated evacuee stations or accessible stations in an outer envelope (s.116Y12(c)). CEC guide: outer envelopes are checked so no one voted twice, then counted by Counting Committees 'located within the Knesset'. Basic Law: The Knesset s.11: results published 'within eight days'. 2022: 'all the regular ballots ... counted by just after noon' on 2 Nov, after which the CEC 'moved on to the counting of some 500,000 double envelopes' (The Media Line, 2 Nov 2022, https://themedialine.org/?p=134483). For 27 Oct 2026: regular count expected by midday 28 Oct, envelopes after that (estimate by analogy); statutory publication deadline 4 Nov.

findings.claim: Double envelopes lean strongly away from Arab and haredi lists and toward right-religious lists; the lean is large in percentage points and stable in sign across five elections.
findings.quant: Double-envelope share minus regular-station share (pp, CEC): Arab lists - Joint List 2019s -6.75, 2020 -7.70, 2021 -2.40; Hadash-Ta'al 2019a -2.89, 2022 -2.26; Ra'am(-Balad) 2019a -2.29, 2021 -2.45, 2022 -2.57; Balad 2022 -1.46. Haredi - UTJ -2.0 to -2.6 every cycle; Shas -0.6 to -1.9. Right-religious - Zehut 2019a +4.09; URWP/Yamina +0.88 (2019a), +3.18, +3.34, +3.54 (2019s-2021); RZ 2021 +1.45, 2022 +5.10. Likud +2.9 to +3.5 in 2019-2020, ~0 in 2021-2022. Labor 2021 +2.25, 2022 +1.58; Meretz -0.2 to +0.7. Matches the IDI characterisation (young Jewish voters; favour right-wing and fringe lists; disadvantage haredi and Arab lists).

source.authors: Times of Israel staff, reporting an IDI analysis by Or Anabi and Ofer Kenig
source.title: Why the remaining ballots are likely to sink Balad, confirm Netanyahu's victory

findings.model_link: Election-night engine; dossier s.2 double-envelope lean bullet ('haredi and Arab lists ~1/3-1/2 under their regular-station share') - supported for Arab lists (34-52% of their regular-station share), weaker for haredi lists (UTJ 56-67%, Shas 69-92%).
findings.site_use: Double envelopes skew young and Jewish: Arab lists poll a third to a half of their regular-station share in them, haredi lists clearly less, right-religious lists more.

findings.claim: From the complete regular-station count to the final count, seats moved in every election but the net bloc shift was zero in four of five and -1 for the Netanyahu bloc in 2022; the envelope effect is a within-bloc and Arab-list effect, not a +0.5-1 seat drift to the right, and Meretz and Balad (2022) were already below 3.25% before any envelope was opened.
findings.quant: Final minus regular-only seats (statutory allocation with registered pairs, CEC counts): 2019a URWP +1, Likud -1; 2019s B&W +1, Likud +1, UTJ -1, YB -1; 2020 Likud +1, B&W +1, Shas -1, JL -1; 2021 Meretz +1, Ra'am -1; 2022 YB +1, UTJ -1. Straddlers regular% -> final%: Ra'am 2021 4.023 -> 3.788; Ra'am-Balad 2019a 3.461 -> 3.334; New Right 2019a 3.143 -> 3.216 (still short); Labor 2022 3.542 -> 3.694; Meretz 2022 3.169 -> 3.165; Balad 2022 3.049 -> 2.909. (Partial election-night counts differ from the complete regular count; not measured here.)

challenges.title: Threshold denominator: include the unmodelled micro-list vote
challenges.what_literature_says: s.81(a) tests each list against 3.25% of ALL valid votes. In 2015-2022, lists below 0.3% took 0.28-0.85% of valid votes and lists below 0.5% took 0.41-1.49% (CEC). A 0.02-0.03 pp error at the threshold is of the order of real historical misses (New Right 2019a: 1,454 votes).
challenges.current_model: project() (and simulate_core, validate_bayes.allocate_vector) renormalises shares to sum to 1 over the modelled lists, then tests sh >= 0.0325. Since s.42 MICRO_PRIORS is empty, so the 18 unmodelled 2026 lists have zero votes, and the effective threshold is 3.25% x (1 - m) of valid votes. Observation layers disagree on the denominator: seat rows reserve 1% for micro-lists, while CEC filings are renormalised to 1.
challenges.proposed_change: Draw m per simulation from the CEC record of the unmodelled-list share, e.g. lognormal with median 0.5% and a 90% range of 0.3-0.9%, cycle-specific in the harness. Test sh x (1 - m) >= 0.0325, or equivalently compare sh against 0.0325/(1 - m). The D'Hondt allocation among passers is scale-invariant and unchanged. Document which denominator the latent represents.
challenges.how_to_test: Harness: threshold Brier and straddler pass rates on the fidelity windows, with each cycle's actual unmodelled share taken from the CEC expc files, ON vs OFF. Production: change in P(pass) for RZP-Zehut, Ra'am, Otzma and Amcha (expected about -0.2 to -1 pp) and in P(NB>=61).

challenges.title: Harness historical surplus pairs: replace approximations with the registered agreements
challenges.what_literature_says: The registered agreements are on record: CEC notices for 2013-2019s, IDI for 2022, and the pairs that reproduce the official 2021 allocation exactly. With the exact official counts, the statutory allocation under the registered pairs matches the official seats in 6/6 elections. PAST_PAIRS misallocates 8 list-seats, in 2015, 2019s and 2021.
challenges.current_model: validate_model.PAST_PAIRS, labelled 'approximations of the registered agreements'. It is missing YB-Kulanu (2015), B&W-YB (2019s) and Labor-Meretz (2019a, 2021). It includes fictitious B&W-Labor style pairs in 2019a, 2019s and 2021. The dossier lists 'the registered surplus agreements (item 4)' as not built.
challenges.proposed_change: Use the registered pairs. 2015: ZU-Meretz, Likud-JH, UTJ-Shas, YB-Kulanu. 2019a: Labor-Meretz, New Right-YB, Ra'am-Balad-Hadash-Ta'al, Likud-URWP, Shas-UTJ. 2019s: B&W-YB, Likud-Yamina, Labor-Gesher-Democratic Union, UTJ-Shas, Noam-Otzma. 2020: B&W-Labor-Gesher-Meretz, Likud-Yamina, UTJ-Shas. 2021: Likud-RZ, B&W-New Economic, Yamina-New Hope, Yesh Atid-YB, Labor-Meretz, UTJ-Shas. 2022: YA-NU, Labor-Meretz, UTJ-Shas, Likud-RZ. Verify 2009/2013 against full official counts. Apply each pair only in windows after its signing date, which removes the look-ahead the dossier notes.
challenges.how_to_test: Unit test: allocate the CEC final counts per cycle and require equality with the official seats. Harness: re-grade eve/D-7/D-21 seat MAE and coverage. Expected small MAE gains in 2015, 2019s and 2021, of about 0.15-0.3 seats per list in those cycles at the eve.

challenges.title: Correct the seat-law and double-envelope numbers stated on the site and in the dossier
challenges.what_literature_says: On the CEC record 2015-2022: 3-8 remainder-stage seats per election (mean 5.3). Expected pair value about +0.4 seat, a +1 in about a third of cases. Double envelopes were 9.6% of valid votes in 2022 (462,807 cast). The envelopes moved bloc totals by 0 in 4/5 elections and by -1 for the NB in 2022. Meretz and Balad 2022 were below 3.25% on the regular count.
challenges.current_model: Site: pairs 'worth a measured +0.5 to +0.9 expected seats per pair'. Dossier s.1: '~6-9 of 120 seats decided at the surplus stage'. Dossier s.2: 'record 600-700k expected (~12-13%)', 'night->final drift ~+0.5-1 seat right', 'Meretz/Balad 2022 died in the envelopes'.
challenges.proposed_change: Replace them with the measured values in SYS-F05, F07, F17 and F19. Size the election-night engine from the CEC 2022 base (463k), plus the evacuee stations, plus any reservist effect. Model the envelope shift as list-level (Arab and haredi down, right-religious up) rather than as a bloc drift.
challenges.how_to_test: Evidence class: official data (CEC expc files 2019a-2022). Re-run the desk scripts (seatlaw.py, pairvalue.py, night.py) whenever the site text changes.

challenges.title: Statutory fidelity: lottery tie-break and the s.81(d)(4) majority clause (low priority)
challenges.what_literature_says: The law settles a tie in list quotients by a CEC lottery (s.81(d)(2)). It also stops a list that holds half the seats on no more than half the votes from receiving further seats (s.81(d)(4)).
challenges.current_model: dhondt() awards ties to the lowest column index via np.argmax. There is no majority clause.
challenges.proposed_change: Break ties with a seeded random choice and add the 60-seat cap clause, for fidelity only.
challenges.how_to_test: Bit-identical check on harness and production draws (exact ties have probability ~0 with float shares; no 2026 list approaches 50%). Document as verified-no-effect.

open_questions: Which surplus agreements were actually filed by the 16 Oct 2026 deadline? Check against the CEC publication due by 19 Oct (s.67(c)), including any late pairs among sub-threshold lists (Reservists-Economic, Blue and White, Amcha).
How large will the 2026 double-envelope vote be, given the new evacuee stations (ch.10-3C) and reservist mobilisation? No CEC estimate was found.

Why does the election-week figure for 2022 ('over 600,000' double envelopes, ToI/IDI) differ from the CEC's final outer-envelope row (462,807)? Were some special-station ballots tallied outside that row? The full text of Atmor, Friedberg & Kenig (2025) may resolve this.
Do the 2009 and 2013 PAST_PAIRS match the registered agreements? The repo's 2013 CEC file excludes double envelopes, so an exact check needs the full official counts.

Should the latent shares represent valid-vote shares or modelled-pie shares? Seat-derived observations reserve 1% for micro-lists, while CEC filings are renormalised to 1. The threshold fix (challenge 1) depends on the answer.
How does the complete-regular-count to final shift compare with the partial election-night count the public sees? Measuring that needs CEC time-stamped interim releases, which were not located.
